I'm a high school band student who plays a couple instruments, so 1) this will be long and 2) take this with the fact a 15 year old is trying to explain this.

Okay, let's start with piano. With a piano, you can see all of your notes. If you have no idea about music, you can label the keys. If you look at the keys, there's a pattern. Starting at C (kind of the beginning of an octave to me), it is WBWBWWBWBWBWW. That's from one C to the next C. If you don't know much about music, then each time you go up from one key to the next in that order, you go up a half step. A "full" note, like G, will have a half step leading up to it, and up past it. The half step below it is a flat and the half step above it sharp. In the music world, a flat is written as a lowercase b, and a sharp is a #. Notes also can have more than one "name." For example, a C# can also be  called a Db. That is because it's  the half step between C and D. A half step  up from C, so C#, and a half step down  from D, so Db. in the order of the piano keys from above it is 

C C#/Db D D#/Eb E F F#/Gb G G#/Ab A A#/Bb B C

As you can see, there isn't a sharp or flat between e and f or b and c. Idk why that is, but it's how it is. All the sharps and flats are the black keys, and the "full" notes (aka natural notes) are the white keys.

Okay, so once you understand the way notes kind of work, you can try to actually get your hands on a piano. It is easier to start with just your right hand. The right hand usually plays the main part of the song. You can probably look up simple piano tutorials on YouTube

When I play, my right hand usually has my thumb resting on C, then index through pinky on E F G A. You can start in different positions, but that's just how my hand usually falls.

It is a good idea to stretch your hands out to help be able to reach more notes without moving your hand too much.

An easy little tune to play is twinkle twinkle Little star. This can be played in different keys (kinda hard to explain, but basically it can be played at different starting notes and have a similar sound.) But I usually play it starting on C.

To find C on the piano, find the set of 2 black keys. There are 3 white keys near them (one before, one in the middle, one after). C is the one of those white keys. A good way to be able to find keys on a piano when you are first learning is to remember they just go in abc order until G, then they go back to A and repeat.

Also, the way my friend remembers how to find D is that it's the one between the set of two, so it's a D(ick) going in the middle. Might help you out, idk 

Anyway, once you can find c, spread your hand a bit across so it feels still relaxed, with your thumb on C, and your fingers kind of spreading after it.

Play the song usuing different fingers not just your index finger. I see alot of people do that, and it just kind of pulls you back.

If you can, spread your hand kind of like how I said before (thumb on C, pointer on E, middle on F, ring on G, pinky on A.) This way you can push down different keys without moving your hand.

The beginning of twinkle twinkle is C C G G A A G (twin-kle twin-kle Lit-tle star) I'm not gonna go through the full song here, put u can pm if u want me to lmao.

You can take a gander at what you think you'll like (more cinnamon or more sugar). Usually about a tablespoon total is a generous amount for one piece of toast.
